title.zh: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱
title.en: Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱 Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu

sentences.zh: 高趙田朱

translations.literal: Gao, Zhao, Tian, and Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, Zhao, Tian, and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 高仁厚，亡其系出。

translations.literal: Gao Renhou — his lineage of descent is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou's family origins are unknown.

sentences.zh: 初事劍南西川節度使陳敬瑄為營使。

translations.literal: At first he served Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as camp commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Chen Jingxuan, governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as a camp commissioner.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷京師，天子出居成都，敬瑄遣黃頭軍部將李鋋鞏鹹以兵萬五千戍興平，數敗巢軍。

translations.literal: Huang Chao took the capital; the Son of Heaven went out to dwell at Chengdu; Jingxuan sent the Yellow-Head Army generals Li Xin and Gong Xian with fifteen thousand troops to garrison Xingping, repeatedly defeating Chao's army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao seized the capital, the emperor withdrew to Chengdu. Chen Jingxuan sent Li Xin and Gong Xian of the Yellow-Head Army with fifteen thousand men to hold Xingping, and they defeated Chao's forces again and again.

sentences.zh: 賊號蜀兵為「鵶兒」，每戰，輒戒曰：「毋與鴉兒鬥。

translations.literal: The bandits called the Shu troops "Crow Boys," and before each battle would warn, saying, "Do not fight the crow boys."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels nicknamed the Shu troops "Crow Boys," and before every battle they would warn one another: "Do not fight the crow boys."

sentences.zh: 」敬瑄喜其兵可用，益選卒二千，使仁厚將而東。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was pleased that his troops were usable, selected two thousand more soldiers, and had Renhou lead them east.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan, delighted with their effectiveness, picked out two thousand more troops and sent Renhou east to command them.

sentences.zh: 先是，京師有不肖子，皆著疊帶冒，持梃剽閭裏，號「閑子」。

translations.literal: Previously in the capital there were worthless youths who all wore layered headwraps and turbans, carried clubs and plundered in the lanes, and were called "idlers."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the capital had its share of worthless young men who wore layered headwraps, carried clubs, and robbed their neighborhoods—they were known as "idlers."

sentences.zh: 京兆尹始視事，輒殺尤者以怖其餘。

translations.literal: When a Jingzhao intendant first took office, he would execute the worst offenders to frighten the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new Jingzhao governor took office, he would execute the worst offenders to intimidate the rest.

sentences.zh: 竇潏治京兆，至殺數十百人，稍稍憚戢。

translations.literal: Dou Yun governed Jingzhao and executed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yun governed Jingzhao, he put several hundred to death, and the idlers gradually grew afraid and quieted down.

sentences.zh: 巢入京師，人多避難寶雞，閑子掠之，吏不能制。

translations.literal: When Chao entered the capital, many fled to Baoji for refuge; the idlers plundered them, and officials could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: After Chao took the capital, many people fled to Baoji for safety, but the idlers preyed on them and the authorities could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 仁厚素知狀，下約入邑閭縱擊。

translations.literal: Renhou had long known the situation and issued orders that upon entering towns and lanes they might strike freely.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou had long known how things stood, and he issued orders that his men were free to attack the idlers wherever they found them in the towns.

sentences.zh: 軍入，閑子聚觀嗤侮，於是殺數千人，坊門反閉，欲亡不得，故皆死，自是閭裏乃安。

translations.literal: When the army entered, the idlers gathered to watch and mock; then several thousand were killed; lane gates were shut from within; those wishing to flee could not, so all died — from then on the neighborhoods were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops marched in, the idlers gathered to jeer at them—whereupon thousands were cut down. The lane gates were barred from inside; none could escape, and all perished. From that time the neighborhoods were secure.

sentences.zh: 會邛州賊阡能眾數萬略諸縣，列壁數十，涪州刺史韓秀升等亂峽中，韓求反蜀州，諸將不能定。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Qiongzhou bandit Qian Neng had tens of thousands ravaging the counties and erecting dozens of stockades; Fuzhou prefect Han Xiushan and others stirred trouble in the gorges; Han Qiu rebelled at Shuzhou — the generals could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: About this time the Qiongzhou rebel Qian Neng led tens of thousands in plundering the counties and building dozens of fortified camps. Han Xiushan, prefect of Fuzhou, and others raised havoc in the gorges, while Han Qiu rebelled at Shuzhou, and none of the generals could put them down.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄召仁厚還，使督兵四討，屯永安。

translations.literal: Jingxuan recalled Renhou and had him supervise troops on four fronts, encamped at Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan recalled Renhou and put him in charge of forces on four fronts, with headquarters at Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 阡能遣諜者入軍中，吏執以獻，諜自言父母妻子囚於賊，約不得軍虛實且死。

translations.literal: Qian Neng sent spies into the army; officers seized and presented them; the spies said their parents, wives, and children were held prisoner by the bandits, bound by pact to report the army's strength and weakness or die.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng sent spies into the camp. When officers captured them and brought them in, the spies explained that the rebels held their families hostage and had sworn them to report on the army's movements—or face death.

sentences.zh: 仁厚哀之，曰：「為我報賊，明日我且戰，有能釋甲迎我者，署背曰『歸順』，皆得復農矣。

translations.literal: Renhou pitied them and said, "Go tell the bandits for me: tomorrow I shall fight; whoever can cast off armor to welcome me — have 'Submitted' written on the back — all may return to farming."
translations.idiomatic: Renhou took pity on them and said, "Tell the rebels for me: I attack tomorrow. Whoever lays down his arms to welcome me—let him have 'Submitted' marked on his back—and he may go home to his fields."

sentences.zh: 」縱諜去，命諸將毀柵，鼓而前。

translations.literal: He released the spies, ordered the generals to tear down the stockades, and beat the drums to advance.
translations.idiomatic: He let the spies go, ordered his generals to tear down the stockades, and marched forward to the beat of the drums.

sentences.zh: 賊渠羅渾擎設伏詐降，仁厚遣將不持兵入諭其眾，皆真降。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Luo Hunqing set an ambush and feigned surrender; Renhou sent officers without weapons to address the masses, and all truly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Luo Hunqing laid an ambush and pretended to surrender. Renhou sent officers in unarmed to reason with the men, and they submitted in earnest.

sentences.zh: 渾擎詐窮而逸，吏執之，仁厚曰：「愚人不足語。

translations.literal: Hunqing feigned exhaustion and fled; officers seized him; Renhou said, "A fool is not worth addressing."
translations.idiomatic: Hunqing pretended to be at his last gasp and slipped away, but officers caught him. Renhou said, "This fool is not worth talking to."

sentences.zh: 」降眾署，皆得免，則告諸壁：「大軍至。

translations.literal: The surrendered masses were registered and all exempted; then he announced to the other stockades, "The great army has arrived."
translations.idiomatic: He registered those who had surrendered and granted them all amnesty, then sent word to the other camps: "The main army is here."

sentences.zh: 」賊帥句胡僧大驚，斬之，莫能禁，眾執胡僧以降。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gou Huseng was greatly alarmed and beheaded someone, but could not restrain them; the crowd seized Huseng and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Gou Huseng panicked and began executing men, but could not hold them back; the troops seized Huseng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 韓求知大賊已禽，徇諸壁曰：「敢出者斬！

translations.literal: Han Qiu, learning the great bandit had been captured, paraded the stockades saying, "Whoever dares come out shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: When Han Qiu learned that the chief rebel had been taken, he rode through the camps proclaiming, "Anyone who comes out will be killed!"

sentences.zh: 」眾罵之，求赴水死，眾鉤出，斬以徇，余柵皆下。

translations.literal: The crowd cursed him; Qiu sought death by drowning; the crowd hooked him out, beheaded him as a warning, and the remaining stockades all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The men cursed him. Qiu tried to drown himself, but they hauled him out with hooks, beheaded him as an example, and the rest of the stockades surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仁厚按轡徘徊視賊壘，吏請焚之，仁厚命取財糧，乃縱火，屍賊成都。

translations.literal: Renhou held the reins and rode about surveying the bandit camps; officers asked to burn them; Renhou ordered goods and grain taken first, then set fire; corpses piled at Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou rode slowly about the rebel strongholds. When his officers asked to burn them, he ordered the spoils and grain removed first, then set them ablaze. The dead were heaped at Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 仁厚還，天子禦樓勞軍，授仁厚檢校尚書左仆射、眉州刺史。

translations.literal: When Renhou returned, the Son of Heaven appeared atop the gate-tower to reward the army and appointed Renhou Acting Minister of the Left and Governor of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On Renhou's return, the emperor appeared on the gate-tower to honor the army and appointed him Acting Minister of the Left and governor of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄與仁厚謀曰：「秀升未禽，貢輸梗奪，百官乏奉，民不鹽食。

translations.literal: Jingxuan counseled Renhou, saying, "Xiushan is not yet captured; tribute and transport are blocked; the hundred officials lack stipends; the people have no salt to eat."
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan said to Renhou in counsel, "Xiushan is still at large; tribute and supplies are cut off; the court officials go unpaid; the people cannot even get salt."

sentences.zh: 公能破賊，當以東川待公。

translations.literal: If you can defeat the bandits, Eastern Chuan shall await you.
translations.idiomatic: If you can break the rebels, Eastern Chuan is yours.

sentences.zh: 」仁厚許之。

translations.literal: Renhou agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔拜行軍司馬。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him mobile army inspector.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him mobile army inspector.

sentences.zh: 仁厚聞賊儲械、子女皆在屯，乃以銳兵瀕江，伐木頹水礙舟道，負岸而陣。

translations.literal: Renhou heard the bandits' stored weapons and women and children were all in the camp; he led crack troops along the river, felled trees to collapse into the water and obstruct the shipping lanes, and arrayed along the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the rebels had stockpiled arms and families in their camp, Renhou took elite troops to the riverbank, felled trees into the stream to block the boats, and drew up his line along the shore.

sentences.zh: 使遊軍逼賊，久不戰，則夜以千卒持短刀、強弩直薄營，火而噪之。

translations.literal: He sent raiding parties to press the bandits; when they fought not for long, at night a thousand men with short swords and strong crossbows pressed straight against the camp, set fire, and raised a clamor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent skirmishers to harry the enemy. When they held back from battle, he sent a thousand men at night with short swords and powerful crossbows to rush the camp, set it ablaze, and raise a great uproar.

sentences.zh: 秀升率舟兵救火，仁厚遣人鶩沒鑿舟，皆沈，眾懼，多潰。

translations.literal: Xiushan led boat soldiers to fight the fire; Renhou sent men diving like ducks to bore holes in the boats — all sank; the masses panicked and mostly fled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushan led his river troops to fight the blaze, but Renhou had divers bore holes in the boats until every vessel sank. The rebels panicked and broke in flight.

sentences.zh: 秀升斬潰兵，欲脅止之，眾怒，執秀升以降。

translations.literal: Xiushan beheaded fleeing soldiers, wishing to coerce them into halting; the troops grew angry, seized Xiushan, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiushan began killing fleeing soldiers to force the rest to stand firm, but his men grew furious, seized him, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仁厚問狀，對曰：「天子蒙塵，反者何獨我？

translations.literal: Renhou questioned him; he replied, "The Son of Heaven suffers exile in the dust — why should I alone be a rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: When Renhou questioned him, Xiushan answered, "The emperor is driven into exile—why should I alone be called a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」仁厚檻車送行在，斬於市。

translations.literal: Renhou sent him in a caged cart to the imperial encampment and executed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent him to the emperor's camp in a cage and had him beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使楊師立初隸神策軍，累遷檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had early served in the Divine Strategy Army and rose repeatedly to Acting Grand Preceptor and equal to ministers of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili, governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Divine Strategy Army and risen through repeated promotions to Acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 聞敬瑄仁厚代己，有望言。

translations.literal: Hearing that Jingxuan and Renhou would replace him, he spoke with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Chen Jingxuan intended to replace him with Renhou, he spoke bitterly of it.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄諷帝召師立以本官兼尚書右仆射，師立益怒，移檄言敬瑄十罪，殺監軍田繪，屯涪城，遣兵攻綿州，不克。

translations.literal: Jingxuan hinted to the Emperor to summon Shili with his existing office plus Acting Minister of the Right; Shili grew angrier, circulated a proclamation listing ten crimes of Jingxuan, killed supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, sent troops to attack Mianzhou — could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan persuaded the emperor to recall Shili with his present rank plus the post of Acting Minister of the Right. Shili grew still angrier, issued a manifesto listing ten crimes against Chen Jingxuan, killed the supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, and sent troops against Mianzhou without success.

sentences.zh: 又檄劍州刺史姚卓文共攻成都，假卓文為指揮應接使，卓文不應。

translations.literal: He also circulated a call to Jianzhou prefect Yao Zhuowen to attack Chengdu jointly, appointing Zhuowen commanding liaison officer; Zhuowen did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He also summoned Yao Zhuowen, prefect of Jianzhou, to join in an attack on Chengdu and named him liaison commander, but Zhuowen refused.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔削官爵。

translations.literal: The Emperor then issued an edict stripping his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict stripping him of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄即表仁厚為東川節度留後，楊茂言為行軍副使，楊棠為諸軍都虞候，率兵三萬討之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan immediately memorialized Renhou as Eastern Chuan military governor designate, Yang Maoyan as mobile deputy, Yang Tang as chief military inspector of all armies, and led thirty thousand troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan at once recommended Renhou as acting governor of Eastern Chuan, Yang Maoyan as mobile deputy, and Yang Tang as chief inspector of all armies, and marched thirty thousand men against Shili.

sentences.zh: 師立遣大將張士安、鄭君雄守鹿頭關。

translations.literal: Shili sent his great generals Zhang Shi'an and Zheng Junxiong to hold Lutou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shili sent his chief generals Zhang Shi'an and Zheng Junxiong to defend Lutou Pass.

sentences.zh: 仁厚次漢州，前軍戰德陽，師立嬰城，閱四旬，夜出兵擾北柵，仁厚設兩翼而伏，披柵門列炬，賊不敢進，伏發，擊走之。

translations.literal: Renhou halted at Hanzhou; the vanguard fought at Deyang; Shili defended the city — after forty days, at night he sent troops to harass the northern stockade; Renhou set wings in ambush, broke open the stockade gates and lined torches; the bandits dared not advance; the ambush sprang and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou encamped at Hanzhou while his vanguard fought at Deyang. Shili shut himself in the city. After forty days he sent a night raid against the northern camp. Renhou posted wings in ambush, threw open the stockade gates, and lined torches along the way. The enemy dared not advance; when the ambush struck, they were driven off.

sentences.zh: 楊茂言謂仁厚且敗，引兵走，久乃還。

translations.literal: Yang Maoyan said Renhou would surely be defeated and led troops in flight, returning only after a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Maoyan decided Renhou was about to lose and withdrew with his troops, returning only after a long delay.

sentences.zh: 明日，會諸將，仁厚曰：「副使當以死報天子。

translations.literal: The next day, at the assembly of generals, Renhou said, "The deputy should die to repay the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he convened his generals and said, "The deputy must pay with his life for his failure to serve the emperor."

sentences.zh: 」斬而徇。

translations.literal: He beheaded him as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded as an example to the army.

sentences.zh: 於是士安不敢出，師立自督士，十戰皆北。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi'an dared not emerge; Shili himself supervised the troops — ten battles, all defeats.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shi'an dared not come out, and though Shili personally led his men in ten engagements, he was beaten every time.

sentences.zh: 仁厚約城中斬首惡者賞，君雄呼於軍曰：「天子所討，反者耳，吾等何與？

translations.literal: Renhou offered a pact: whoever in the city beheaded the chief villains would be rewarded; Junxiong shouted to the army, "What the Son of Heaven punishes is rebels alone — what have we to do with it?"
translations.idiomatic: Renhou promised rewards to anyone in the city who killed the ringleaders. Junxiong cried out to the troops, "The emperor is punishing rebels—what is that to us?"

sentences.zh: 」乃與士安嘩而進，以仁厚書示師立曰：「請以死謝眾。

translations.literal: Then he and Shi'an clamored and advanced, showing Shili Renhou's letter and saying, "Please die to apologize to the masses."
translations.idiomatic: He and Shi'an then stormed forward with an uproar, showed Shili Renhou's letter, and said, "You must die to satisfy the men."

sentences.zh: 」自沈於池死。

translations.literal: He drowned himself in a pool.
translations.idiomatic: Shili drowned himself in a pool.

sentences.zh: 君雄悉誅其家，獻首天子。

translations.literal: Junxiong executed all his family and presented the head to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong put Shili's entire family to death and sent his head to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仁厚入府，縱系囚，賑貧絕。

translations.literal: Renhou entered the prefectural seat, released prisoners, and relieved the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou entered the prefectural seat, freed the prisoners, and gave relief to the poorest families.

sentences.zh: 詔拜劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，遂據梓州，絕敬瑄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi he then seized Zizhou and broke with Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi (886) he seized Zizhou and cut off relations with Chen Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 君雄時為遂州刺史，亦陷漢州，攻成都。

translations.literal: Junxiong was then Governor of Suizhou; he also took Hanzhou and attacked Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong, who was now governor of Suizhou, also seized Hanzhou and marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄使部將李順之逆戰，君雄死。

translations.literal: Jingxuan sent his officer Li Shunzhi to meet them in battle; Junxiong died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan sent his officer Li Shunzhi to meet him in battle, and Junxiong was killed.

sentences.zh: 又發維、茂州羌軍擊仁厚，斬之。

translations.literal: He also sent Wei and Mao prefecture Qiang troops to attack Renhou and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan also sent Qiang troops from Wei and Mao prefectures against Renhou and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，皆追贈司徒。

translations.literal: During Qianning, all were posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning era, they were all posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 趙犨，陳州宛丘人，世為忠武軍牙將。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou was a native of Wancheng in Chenzhou; for generations his family served as military tooth generals of the Loyal and Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou was a native of Wancheng in Chen Prefecture. For generations his family had served as officers of the Loyal and Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 犨資警健，兒弄時好為營陣行列，自號令指顧，群兒無敢亂。

translations.literal: Chou was by nature alert and sturdy; as a child at play he liked to form camp arrays and ranks, himself issuing commands and gestures — the other boys dared not disorder themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was quick-witted and robust. Even as a boy at play he liked to drill his companions in battle formations, giving orders and directing them, and none of the others dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 父叔文見之，曰：「是當大吾門。

translations.literal: His father Shuwén saw it and said, "This one will enlarge our house."
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuwén saw this and said, "This boy will bring greatness to our clan."

sentences.zh: 」稍長，喜書，學擊劍，善射。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he loved books, studied swordplay, and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he took to books, studied swordsmanship, and became an expert archer.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從伐潞州，收天井關，又從征蠻，忠武軍功多，遷大校。

translations.literal: During Huichang he followed the campaign against Luzhou, took Tianjing Pass, and again followed the expedition against the barbarians; the Loyal and Martial Army's achievements were many, and he was promoted to senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang era he joined the campaign against Luzhou and helped take Tianjing Pass, then served in the southern campaigns. The Loyal and Martial Army won great distinction, and he was promoted to senior commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入長安，所在盜興，陳人詣節度府，請犨為刺史，表於朝，授之。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao entered Chang'an, banditry rose everywhere; the people of Chen went to the circuit headquarters, asked that Chou be made prefect, memorialized the court, and he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao entered Chang'an, brigandage broke out everywhere. The people of Chen went to the circuit headquarters and asked that Chou be made their prefect. The request was sent to court, and he was appointed.

sentences.zh: 既視事，會官屬計曰：「巢若不死長安，必東出關，陳其沖也。

translations.literal: Once he took office, he convened the officials and staff and said, "If Chao does not die in Chang'an, he will surely march east out of the passes — Chen is the strategic choke point."
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he gathered his staff and said, "If Chao is not destroyed in Chang'an, he will surely march east through the passes—and Chen lies directly in his path."

sentences.zh: 」乃培城疏塹，實倉庫，峙槁薪，為守計。

translations.literal: He then heightened the walls, cleared the moats, filled the storehouses, stockpiled firewood, and made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the walls, deepened the moats, filled the granaries, piled up fuel, and made every preparation for a siege.

sentences.zh: 民有貲者悉內之，繕甲兵，募悍勇，悉補子弟領兵。

translations.literal: Wealthy civilians were all brought inside; he repaired armor and weapons, recruited fierce braves, and all were appointed with his sons and younger kinsmen leading the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He brought every wealthy household inside the walls, repaired arms and armor, recruited the bravest men, and put his sons and kinsmen in command of them all.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，果東奔。

translations.literal: Chao was defeated and indeed fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao was defeated, he fled east as expected.

sentences.zh: 賊將孟楷以萬人寇項，犨擊禽之。

translations.literal: The bandit general Meng Kai with ten thousand men raided Xiang; Chou attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Meng Kai invaded Xiang with ten thousand men, but Chou attacked and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嘉其功，遷累檢校司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong commended his achievement and promoted him in stages to Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 巢聞楷死，驚且怒，悉軍據溵水，與秦宗權合兵數十萬，繚長壕五周，百道攻之。

translations.literal: Chao heard Kai was dead, was shocked and angry, gathered all his army and held the Yin River, joined forces with Qin Zongquan to several hundred thousand, ringed long trenches five circuits deep, and attacked on a hundred fronts.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao learned of Kai's death he was stunned and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of several hundred thousand, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and attacked on every side.

sentences.zh: 州人大恐，犨令曰：「士貴建功立名節，今雖眾寡不敵，男子當死地求生，徒懼無益也。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were greatly afraid; Chou ordered, saying, "Gentlemen value establishing merit and preserving reputation; though now few cannot match many, men should seek life from the place of death — mere fear is of no use."
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture were terrified. Chou proclaimed, "A true soldier wins fame by deeds of valor. We are outnumbered, but a man finds life by fighting where death seems certain. Fear alone will save no one."

sentences.zh: 且死國，不愈生為賊乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, to die for the state — is it not better than living as bandits?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not better to die for one's country than to live on as a rebel's slave?

sentences.zh: 吾家食陳祿，誓破賊以保陳，異議者斬！

translations.literal: My family has eaten Chen's stipends — I swear to break the bandits and preserve Chen; whoever disagrees shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: My family has lived on Chen's bounty. I swear to break the rebels and save this city—and anyone who disagrees will be executed!

sentences.zh: 」眾聽命。

translations.literal: The crowd obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The men obeyed.

sentences.zh: 引銳士出戰，屢破賊。

translations.literal: He led crack troops out to battle and repeatedly defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He led his best troops out to fight and defeated the rebels again and again.

sentences.zh: 巢益怒，將必屠之，乃起八仙營於州左，僭象宮闕，列百官曹署，儲糧為持久計。

translations.literal: Chao grew angrier and intended to slaughter the city; he then raised the Eight Immortals Camp to the left of the prefecture, presumptuously imitating palace halls, arrayed the hundred officials' offices, and stored grain for a prolonged campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Chao grew still angrier and resolved to slaughter the city. He built the Eight Immortals Camp east of the walls, laid out quarters in imitation of the imperial palace, set up offices for his officials, and stockpiled grain for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 宗權輸鎧仗軍須，賊益張。

translations.literal: Zongquan supplied armor, weapons, and military provisions; the bandits grew still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan sent armor, weapons, and supplies, and the rebels grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 犨小大數百戰，勝負相當，故人心固，乃間道乞師於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Chou fought great and small engagements several hundred times, victories and defeats roughly equal; therefore popular resolve held firm; he then sent by secret path to beg troops from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chou fought hundreds of engagements large and small, winning about as often as he lost, and the people's resolve held firm. He sent a secret messenger to Zhu Quanzhong begging for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴軍至，壁西北，陳人思奮，犨引兵急擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Before long the Bian army arrived and encamped northwest; the people of Chen were eager to fight; Chou led troops in a swift attack on the bandits and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Bian troops arrived and camped to the northwest. The people of Chen were eager to fight. Chou led a fierce assault and routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 圍凡三百日而解。

translations.literal: The siege lasted in all three hundred days before it was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three hundred days before it was finally lifted.

sentences.zh: 中和五年，擢彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhonghe he was promoted to military governor of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhonghe (885) he was appointed military governor of the Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 巢雖敗，宗權始熾，略地數千里，屠二十餘州，唯陳賴犨獨完，以功檢校司徒，加泰寧、浙西兩節度，皆在陳並領之。

translations.literal: Though Chao was defeated, Zongquan then flourished, overrunning territory several thousand li and slaughtering more than twenty prefectures — only Chen, relying on Chou, remained intact; for his merit he was made Acting Grand Preceptor, with the two circuits of Taining and Zhexi added, all administered from Chen concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Although Chao was defeated, Qin Zongquan rose to power, ravaging thousands of li of territory and laying waste to more than twenty prefectures. Chen alone, thanks to Chou, stood intact. For this he was made Acting Grand Preceptor and given the additional commands of Taining and Zhexi, all administered from Chen.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進同中書門下平章事、忠武軍節度，仍治陳州，流亡踵還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was advanced to equal to ministers of state and military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army, still governing Chenzhou; exiles returned in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longji era (889) he was made co-equal with the chief ministers and military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army, still ruling from Chenzhou, and refugees began streaming home.

sentences.zh: 與弟昶至友愛，後將老，悉以軍事付之，乃卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He and his younger brother Chang were deeply affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him, then died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Chang were devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 犨悉忠力以孤城抗賊，巢卒敗亡。

translations.literal: Chou exhausted loyalty and strength to resist the bandits with a lone city, and Chao ultimately was defeated and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Chou had poured all his loyalty and strength into holding a single city against the rebels, and in the end Chao was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 然附全忠，亦賴其力復振，故委輸調發助全忠，常先它鎮雲。

translations.literal: Yet he attached himself to Quanzhong and also relied on his strength to revive; therefore he entrusted transport and dispatch to aid Quanzhong, often ahead of other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had thrown in his lot with Zhu Quanzhong and depended on Zhu's power to recover his position, so he sent supplies and troops to aid him, often ahead of every other circuit.

sentences.zh: 昶，字大東，神采軒異，而內沈厚，有法度。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Dadong, had a lofty and striking bearing, yet inwardly was deep and steady, with a sense of measure.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, styled Dadong, had a striking presence, yet inwardly he was grave and steady and governed by strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 破孟楷功多。

translations.literal: In defeating Meng Kai his achievements were great.
translations.idiomatic: He won great distinction in the defeat of Meng Kai.

sentences.zh: 巢之圍，昶夜掫師，疲而寢，如有神相之者。

translations.literal: During Chao's siege, Chang led troops by night; weary, he slept, as if spirits aided him.
translations.idiomatic: During Chao's siege Chang led the troops by night. Exhausted, he fell asleep on watch, yet it was as though spirits watched over him.

sentences.zh: 犁曙決戰，士爭奮死鬥，禽賊酋數人，斬級千餘。

translations.literal: At daybreak he fought a decisive battle; the soldiers strove in desperate combat; several bandit chiefs were captured and more than a thousand heads were cut.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fought a decisive battle. The men fought with desperate valor, captured several rebel chiefs, and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 犨領泰寧，以昶為州刺史、檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: Chou held Taining and appointed Chang Governor of the prefecture and Acting Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: While Chou held Taining, he appointed Chang prefect of the circuit and Acting Minister of the Right.

sentences.zh: 當時，方鎮言忠壯吏治，舉言犨、昶。

translations.literal: At the time, when the regional commanders spoke of loyalty, valor, and administrative governance, they all cited Chou and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time, whenever the regional governors spoke of loyalty, courage, and good administration, they named Chou and Chang.

sentences.zh: 犨之老，乃授留後，遷忠武節度使，亦留陳。

translations.literal: When Chou grew old, he was made acting governor; he was transferred to military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army and also remained at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou grew old he made Chang his acting governor, then transferred the Loyal and Martial command to him while remaining at Chen.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 劭勸農桑，於人有恩惠。

translations.literal: He exhorted agriculture and sericulture and showed kindness to the people.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged farming and sericulture and treated the people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was added as equal to ministers of state.
translations.idiomatic: He was made co-equal with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年卒，年五十三，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning he died, aged fifty-three, and was posthumously made Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qianning (895), aged fifty-three, and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 犨子珝，字有節。

translations.literal: Chou's son Xu, style name Youjie.
translations.idiomatic: Chou's son Xu, styled Youjie.

sentences.zh: 雄毅喜書，善騎射。

translations.literal: Bold and resolute, he loved books and was skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resolute, he loved learning and excelled at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 巢之難，激勵麾下，約皆死。

translations.literal: During Chao's calamity, he exhorted and encouraged his subordinates, pledging that all would die.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao's siege he roused his men and bound them by oath to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 以先冢邇賊，畏見殘齮，即夜縋死士取柩以入。

translations.literal: Because the ancestral tombs were near the bandits, fearing they would be seen desecrated and gnawed, that very night he lowered daredevils by rope to bring the coffins inside.
translations.idiomatic: The family graves lay close to the enemy lines, and he feared they would be defiled. That night he sent daredevils down on ropes to bring the coffins within the walls.

sentences.zh: 庫有巨弩，機牙壞，不能張，珝以意調治，激矢至五百步，人馬皆洞，賊畏不敢逼。

translations.literal: In the storehouse was a great crossbow whose trigger mechanism was broken and could not be drawn; Xu repaired it by intuition; released arrows reached five hundred paces, piercing men and horses through; the bandits feared and dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: In the arsenal stood a great crossbow with a broken mechanism that no one could draw. Xu restored it by instinct alone. Its bolts pierced men and horses five hundred paces away, and the rebels dared not come near.

sentences.zh: 以勞檢校尚書右仆射，遙領處州刺史。

translations.literal: For his merit he was made Acting Minister of the Right and held the governorship of Chuzhou from afar.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was appointed Acting Minister of the Right and given the governorship of Chuzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 昶帥忠武，珝遷行軍司馬。

translations.literal: When Chang commanded the Loyal and Martial Army, Xu was transferred to mobile army inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took command of the Loyal and Martial Army, Xu was made mobile army inspector.

sentences.zh: 昶之喪，知忠武留後，政簡濟，上下安之。

translations.literal: At Chang's funeral he became acting governor of the Loyal and Martial Army; his administration was simple and effective, and high and low were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang's death he became acting governor of the Loyal and Martial Army. His rule was simple and effective, and officers and men alike were content.

sentences.zh: 全忠表為忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized him as military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recommended him for the post of military governor of the Loyal and Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 陳土惡善圮，珝疊甓表墉，遂無患。

translations.literal: Chen soil was poor and prone to collapse; Xu laid brick facing on the walls and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The soil of Chen was weak and the walls often crumbled. Xu faced them with layered brick and the problem ceased.

sentences.zh: 三加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Three times he was added as Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was three times promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，同中書門下平章事，進兼侍中，封天水郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua he was made equal to ministers of state, advanced concurrently to Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guanghua he was made co-equal with the chief ministers, promoted to Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 按鄧艾故跡，決翟王渠溉稻以利農。

translations.literal: Following Deng Ai's old traces, he opened the Zhaiwang Canal to irrigate rice fields for the benefit of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Following the route of Deng Ai's old canal, he opened the Zhaiwang Channel to irrigate the rice fields and benefit the farmers.

sentences.zh: 一家三節度，相繼二十餘年，陳人宜之。

translations.literal: One family with three military governors in succession for more than twenty years — the people of Chen found it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: One family held three governorships in succession for more than twenty years, and the people of Chen thought it only right.

sentences.zh: 天復初，韓建帥忠武，以珝知同州節度留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Loyal and Martial Army and made Xu acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, Han Jian took command of the Loyal and Martial Army and appointed Xu acting governor of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還長安，詔入朝，賜號「迎鑾功臣」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, he was summoned to court and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang'an, Xu was summoned to court and given the title Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.

sentences.zh: 以檢校太傅為右金吾衛上將軍，從東遷。

translations.literal: As Acting Grand Tutor he was made commanding general of the Right Golden Guard and followed the eastern relocation.
translations.idiomatic: As Acting Grand Tutor he was appointed commanding general of the Right Golden Guard and accompanied the court's move east.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was relieved due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈侍中，陳人為罷市。

translations.literal: He died, aged fifty-five, posthumously made Palace Attendant; the people of Chen closed their markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously made Palace Attendant. The people of Chen closed their markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 田頵，字德臣，廬州合肥人。

translations.literal: Tian Jun, style name Dechen, was a native of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun, styled Dechen, was a native of Hefei in Luz Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 略通書傳，沈果有大誌。

translations.literal: He had some knowledge of books and records, was deep and resolute, and had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning in the classics, was grave and resolute, and harbored great ambition.

sentences.zh: 與楊行密同裏，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: He was from the same village as Yang Xingmi and they pledged to be as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He came from the same village as Yang Xingmi, and the two pledged themselves as brothers.

sentences.zh: 應州募屯邊，遷主將。

translations.literal: He answered the prefecture's call to garrison the frontier and was promoted to chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: He answered the prefecture's call to garrison the frontier and rose to chief commander.

sentences.zh: 行密據廬州，頵謀為多。

translations.literal: When Xingmi held Luzhou, Jun's stratagems were the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: When Xingmi seized Luzhou, Jun's counsel proved the most valuable.

sentences.zh: 攻趙锽於宣州，锽出東溪，乘暴流以逸，阻水解甲，謂追騎不能及。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhao Chou at Xuanzhou, Chou went out by East Stream, rode the violent current to escape, blocked the water to remove armor, thinking the pursuing horsemen could not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Zhao Chou at Xuanzhou, Chou fled down the East Stream and rode the raging current to safety. He dammed the water, laid aside his armor, and thought his pursuers could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 頵乘輕舠追之，锽驚，遂見禽。

translations.literal: Jun pursued in a light boat; Chou was alarmed and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jun pursued in a light skiff. Chou panicked and was taken.

sentences.zh: 行密表頵為馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Xingmi memorialized Jun as chief military inspector of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi recommended Jun for the post of chief inspector of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 沙陀叛將安仁義奔淮南，行密大喜，屬以騎兵，使在頵右，兩人名冠軍中，共攻常州，殺刺史杜棱。

translations.literal: The Shatuo rebel An Renyi fled to Huainan; Xingmi was greatly pleased, entrusted him with cavalry, placed him on Jun's right; the two men's fame topped the army; together they attacked Changzhou and killed prefect Du Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo defector An Renyi fled to Huainan. Xingmi was delighted and gave him command of the cavalry, posting him at Jun's right hand. The two were the foremost warriors in the army. Together they attacked Changzhou and killed the prefect Du Ling.

sentences.zh: 錢镠方屯潤州，一夕潰。

translations.literal: Qian Liu was then encamped at Runzhou; in one night he was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu was encamped at Runzhou, but in a single night his army was routed.

sentences.zh: 會孫儒南略，頵等屯丹陽，儒火揚州，壁廣德，頵破其屯。

translations.literal: When Sun Ru marched south, Jun and others encamped at Danyang; Ru burned Yangzhou and walled Guangde; Jun broke his camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ru marched south, Jun and the others encamped at Danyang. Ru burned Yangzhou and fortified Guangde, but Jun overran his camp.

sentences.zh: 與戰，頵走，行密怒，奪其兵。

translations.literal: In battle Jun fled; Xingmi was angry and stripped him of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Jun fled. Xingmi was furious and stripped him of his command.

sentences.zh: 或諫行密曰：「強敵傅壘，不用頵，非計也。

translations.literal: Someone advised Xingmi, saying, "With a strong foe pressing the camp, not using Jun is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xingmi, saying, "With a powerful enemy at the gates, to leave Jun idle is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 」行密復將頵。

translations.literal: Xingmi again placed Jun in command.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi put Jun back in command.

sentences.zh: 儒詒書仁義通好，以疑行密，行密待益厚，署行軍副使，卒用此二人功禽儒。

translations.literal: Ru sent a deceitful letter to Renyi proposing friendship to sow doubt in Xingmi; Xingmi treated him still more generously, appointed him mobile deputy, and in the end used these two men's merit to capture Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ru sent a forged letter to Renyi proposing an alliance, hoping to sow suspicion. Xingmi treated Renyi all the more generously and made him mobile deputy. In the end it was these two men's valor that captured Ru.

sentences.zh: 乃表仁義為潤州刺史，頵寧國軍節度使。

translations.literal: He then memorialized Renyi as Governor of Runzhou and Jun as military governor of the Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Renyi as governor of Runzhou and Jun as military governor of the Ningguo Army.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and equal to ministers of state.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and co-equal with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 仁義至檢校太保。

translations.literal: Renyi rose to Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi rose to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 頵已平馮弘鐸，至揚州謝行密。

translations.literal: After Jun had pacified Feng Hongduo, he came to Yangzhou to thank Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun had pacified Feng Hongduo, he came to Yangzhou to pay his respects to Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 左右求貲不已，獄吏亦有請，頵怒曰：「吏覬吾入獄邪！

translations.literal: Attendants kept asking for gifts without end; prison officers also made requests; Jun angrily said, "Do the clerks expect to see me in prison?"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants kept demanding gifts without end, and even the prison officers asked for bribes. Jun snapped, "Do these clerks expect to see me behind bars?"

sentences.zh: 」又求池、歙為屬州，行密不許，頵始怨。

translations.literal: He also asked for Chizhou and Shezhou as subordinate prefectures; Xingmi did not permit it; Jun began to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that Chizhou and Shezhou be made his subordinate prefectures. Xingmi refused, and Jun began to harbor resentment.

sentences.zh: 將還，指府門曰：「吾不復入此。」

translations.literal: About to return, he pointed at the prefectural gate and said, "I shall not enter here again."
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to leave, he pointed at the prefectural gate and said, "I shall never set foot in here again."

sentences.zh: 是時，錢镠部將徐綰叛，镠入杭州逐綰，綰屯靈隱山迎頵。

translations.literal: At this time Qian Liu's officer Xu Wan rebelled; Liu entered Hangzhou to drive out Wan; Wan encamped on Lingyin Mountain to welcome Jun.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Qian Liu's officer Xu Wan rebelled. Liu entered Hangzhou to drive him out, but Wan encamped on Lingyin Mountain to welcome Jun.

sentences.zh: 頵遣客何曉見镠曰：「王宜東保會稽，無為虛屠士眾也。

translations.literal: Jun sent his guest He Xiao to see Liu and say, "Your Highness should guard Kuaiji to the east and not slaughter troops in vain."
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent his envoy He Xiao to tell Liu, "Your Highness should withdraw east to Kuaiji and spare your men a needless slaughter."

sentences.zh: 」镠曰：「軍中小叛常然，公為人長，何助逆耶？

translations.literal: Liu said, "Small rebellions in the army are common; as a man of standing, why aid the traitor?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, "Petty mutinies are common enough in any army. As a man of standing, why do you aid a traitor?"

sentences.zh: 」頵攻北門，镠登城與語，射中麾下。

translations.literal: Jun attacked the north gate; Liu mounted the wall to speak with him and shot one of Jun's officers.
translations.idiomatic: Jun attacked the north gate. Liu mounted the wall to parley with him and shot one of Jun's officers.

sentences.zh: 頵築壘絕往來道，镠患之，出金幣十輿，募能奪地者。

translations.literal: Jun built stockades cutting the roads; Liu was troubled, sent out ten cartloads of gold and coins, recruiting anyone who could seize the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Jun built fortifications to cut off all traffic. Troubled, Liu offered ten cartloads of gold and coin to anyone who could break the blockade.

sentences.zh: 陳璋以死士三百，免胄馳擊，奪其地，镠授璋衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang with three hundred death-soldiers, bareheaded and charging, seized the ground; Liu appointed Zhang Governor of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang led three hundred daredevils in a bareheaded charge and recaptured the ground. Liu appointed him governor of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 頵攻城未能克，將濟江絕西陵，為镠將所卻，圍益急。

translations.literal: Jun could not take the city by assault; about to cross the river to cut off Xiling, was repelled by Liu's generals; the siege grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Jun could not take the city by assault. He tried to cross the river and cut off Xiling, but Liu's generals drove him back and the siege grew tighter still.

sentences.zh: 先是，行密欲女镠子，镠急，乃遣元迎女，且告行密曰：「頵得誌，為患必大，請以子為質，願召還頵。

translations.literal: Previously Xingmi wished to marry his daughter to Liu's son; Liu was anxious and sent Yuan to welcome the girl, and told Xingmi, "If Jun succeeds, the harm will surely be great; please keep my son as hostage and recall Jun."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingmi had wished to marry his daughter to Liu's son. Liu, anxious, sent Yuan Guangzan to fetch the bride and told Xingmi, "If Jun prevails, the harm will be grave. Keep my son as hostage and recall Jun."

sentences.zh: 」行密使人謂頵曰：「不還，我遣人代守宣州。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent someone to tell Jun, "If you do not return, I shall send someone to replace you at Xuanzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent word to Jun: "If you do not return, I shall send someone else to hold Xuanzhou."

sentences.zh: 」頵不從。

translations.literal: Jun did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 镠輸錢二百萬緡犒軍，頵又請镠子元瓘出質，乃與綰引兵還。

translations.literal: Liu sent two million strings of cash to reward the army; Jun also asked that Liu's son Yuan Guangzan be given as hostage; then he and Wan led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu sent two million strings of cash to reward Jun's army. Jun also demanded that Liu's son Yuan Guangzan be left as hostage. Only then did he and Wan withdraw.

sentences.zh: 然內怨行密與镠，因移書曰：「侯王守方以奉天子，譬百川不朝於海，雖狂奔澶漫，終為涸土，不若順流無窮也。

translations.literal: Yet inwardly he resented Xingmi and Liu, and sent a letter saying, "Princes and marquises guard their regions to serve the Son of Heaven, as the hundred streams must pay court to the sea; though they rush wild and spread vast, in the end they become dry earth — better to follow the current without end."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote, "Princes and lords hold their territories to serve the Son of Heaven, as the hundred streams must flow to the sea. However wildly they may rush and spread, in the end they dry to dust. Better to follow the current without end."

sentences.zh: 東南揚為大，刀布金玉積如阜，願公上天子常賦，頵請悉儲峙，單車以從。

translations.literal: The southeast with Yangzhou greatest, knives, cloth, gold and jade piled like mounds — I wish you to offer the Son of Heaven's regular tribute; Jun requests to store it all and follow with a single cart.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou is the greatest city in the southeast, its stores of goods and gold piled like hills. I urge you to send the emperor his regular tribute—I will store it all and follow behind with a single cart.

sentences.zh: 」行密答曰：「貢賦繇汴而達，適足資敵爾。

translations.literal: Xingmi replied, "Tribute and levies pass through Bian to arrive — that only supplies the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi answered, "Tribute must pass through Bian to reach the capital—that only feeds our enemy."

sentences.zh: 」於是頵絕行密，大募兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Jun broke with Xingmi and recruited troops on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Jun broke with Xingmi and raised a great army.

sentences.zh: 李神福白行密：「頵必叛，宜先圖之。

translations.literal: Li Shenfu told Xingmi, "Jun is sure to rebel; we should plot against him first."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu warned Xingmi, "Jun is certain to rebel. We should strike first."

sentences.zh: 」行密曰：「頵有大功，而反狀未明，殺之，諸將不為用。

translations.literal: Xingmi said, "Jun has great merit, and his rebellion is not yet clear; to kill him — the generals will not serve."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi said, "Jun has rendered great service, and his treason is not yet proven. If we kill him, the other generals will not follow us."

sentences.zh: 」頵遣其佐杜荀鶴至汴通好，全忠喜，屯宿州須變。

translations.literal: Jun sent his aide Du Xunhe to Bian to propose friendship; Quanzhong was pleased and encamped at Suzhou awaiting the change.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent his aide Du Xunhe to Bian to propose an alliance. Zhu Quanzhong was pleased and encamped at Suzhou to await developments.

sentences.zh: 行密以康儒在頵所，故授廬州刺史以間之。

translations.literal: Xingmi because Kang Ru was at Jun's side appointed him Governor of Luzhou to sow discord.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kang Ru was with Jun, Xingmi appointed him governor of Luzhou to sow discord between them.

sentences.zh: 頵怒，族其家，儒曰：「公不用吾謀，死無地矣。」

translations.literal: Jun was angry, exterminated his family; Ru said, "You did not use my counsel — to die there is no ground."
translations.idiomatic: Jun was furious and exterminated Kang's entire family. Kang said, "You would not heed my counsel—now I have nowhere to die."

sentences.zh: 頵與安仁義連和攻升州，劫刺史李神福妻息厚養之。

translations.literal: Jun with An Renyi joined forces to attack Shengzhou, seized prefect Li Shenfu's wife and children and provided for them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Jun allied with An Renyi to attack Shengzhou and seized the wife and children of the prefect Li Shenfu, treating them with every consideration.

sentences.zh: 神福方與劉存攻鄂州，行密召之。

translations.literal: Shenfu was then attacking Ezhou with Liu Cun; Xingmi recalled him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu was then besieging Ezhou with Liu Cun when Xingmi summoned him back.

sentences.zh: 神福謂諸將曰：「頵反，此心腹疾，宜速攻之。

translations.literal: Shenfu told the generals, "Jun has rebelled; this is a disease of the heart and vitals — we should attack swiftly."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu told his officers, "Jun has rebelled. This is a mortal wound—we must attack at once."

sentences.zh: 」頵遣李臯詒書神福曰：「公家在此，茍從我，當分地以王。

translations.literal: Jun sent Li Gao with a deceitful letter to Shenfu, saying, "Your family is here; if you follow me, I shall divide territory and make you a prince."
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent Li Gao with a forged letter to Shenfu: "Your family is in my hands. Follow me and I will divide the realm and make you a prince."

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「吾以一卒從吳王，任上將，終不以妻子易意。

translations.literal: He replied, "I followed the King of Wu with a single soldier, was appointed a great general — I shall never change my mind for wife and children."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu answered, "I followed the King of Wu as a common soldier and rose to high command. I will never betray him for my wife and children."

sentences.zh: 」乃斬臯，破頵兵於曷山。

translations.literal: He then beheaded Gao and defeated Jun's troops at Mount Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Gao and routed Jun's army at Mount Yi.

sentences.zh: 始，頵將王壇等以舟師躡神福後，至吉陽磯，不戰。

translations.literal: Initially Jun's generals Wang Tan and others with naval forces followed Shenfu's rear; reaching Jiyang Ford, they did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: At first Jun's generals Wang Tan and others followed with the fleet. At Jiyang Ford they held back from battle.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，壇掩神福軍半濟，神福反舟順流急擊，大破之，因縱火，士多死。

translations.literal: At dusk Tan ambushed Shenfu's army half across; Shenfu turned his boats downstream and struck swiftly, routing them greatly, then set fire — many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Tan ambushed Shenfu's force mid-crossing. Shenfu turned his boats downstream and struck hard, routing them completely. He then set the fleet ablaze, and many men perished.

sentences.zh: 明日，壇復戰，敗於皖口，頵乃自將來戰。

translations.literal: Next day Tan fought again, was defeated at Wan Estuary; Jun then came in person to fight.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tan fought again and was beaten at Wan Estuary. Jun then took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「賊棄城而來，此天亡也。

translations.literal: Shenfu said, "The bandits abandoned their city to come — this is Heaven's destruction of them."
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said, "The rebels have abandoned their city to come fight us—Heaven has doomed them."

sentences.zh: 」乃瀕水堅壁不出，請行密以兵塞頵走道。

translations.literal: He then held the waterline with stout walls and would not emerge, asking Xingmi to send troops to block Jun's escape route.
translations.idiomatic: He entrenched along the river and refused to give battle, asking Xingmi to send troops to cut off Jun's retreat.

sentences.zh: 仁義焚東塘戰艦，夜攻常州，不克，轉戰至夾岡，立二幟，解甲而息，追兵莫敢向。

translations.literal: Renyi burned the warships at Dongtang, attacked Changzhou by night without success, fought on to Jiagang, set up two banners, removed armor to rest — pursuers dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi burned his warships at Dongtang and attacked Changzhou by night without success. Fighting on to Jiagang, he set up two banners, laid aside his armor to rest, and his pursuers dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 頵陳舟蕪湖。

translations.literal: Jun arrayed boats at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun stationed his fleet at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 行密遣將王茂章攻潤州。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent general Wang Maozhang to attack Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent his general Wang Maozhang to attack Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁義以善射冠軍中，當時稱朱瑾槊，米誌誠弩，皆為第一。

translations.literal: Renyi's skill at archery topped the army; at the time they called Zhu Jin's spear and Mi Zhicheng's crossbow each first in the land.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi was the finest archer in the army. At the time Zhu Jin's spear and Mi Zhicheng's crossbow were each called the best in the realm.

sentences.zh: 仁義常曰：「誌誠弩十，不當瑾槊之一；

translations.literal: Renyi often said, "Ten of Zhicheng's crossbows are not worth one of Jin's spear;"
translations.idiomatic: Renyi used to say, "Ten of Zhicheng's crossbows are not worth one thrust of Jin's spear;"

sentences.zh: 瑾槊十，不當吾弓之一。

translations.literal: ten of Jin's spears are not worth one of my bow."
translations.idiomatic: and ten of Jin's spears are not worth one shot from my bow."

sentences.zh: 」人以為然。

translations.literal: People thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: People believed him.

sentences.zh: 又其治軍嚴，善得士心。

translations.literal: He also governed the army strictly and knew how to win soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also governed his troops with strict discipline and knew how to win their loyalty.

sentences.zh: 戰卒數百，濠梁不毀，開門鬥，先告所當中，然後射之。

translations.literal: In battle several hundred paces apart, the moat and walls unharmed, opening the gate to fight, first announcing what he would hit, then shooting — always hit.
translations.idiomatic: In battle, though hundreds of paces separated the armies and the walls stood intact, he would open the gate to fight. He would announce his target first, then shoot—and never miss.

sentences.zh: 茂章等不敢與確。

translations.literal: Maozhang and others dared not engage him in certainty.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhang and the others dared not meet him in open combat.

sentences.zh: 行密遣使謂曰：「吾不忘公功，能自歸，當復為行軍副使，但不可處兵。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent a messenger saying, "I do not forget your merit; if you return of yourself, you shall again be mobile deputy, but may not hold troops."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent a messenger saying, "I have not forgotten your service. If you surrender of your own accord, you shall again be mobile deputy—but you may not keep command of troops."

sentences.zh: 」仁義欲降，其子固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Renyi wished to surrender; his son strongly remonstrated, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi wished to surrender, but his son pleaded with him urgently, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 行密召其將臺濛泣語曰：「人嘗告頵必反，我不忍負人，頵果負我。

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned his general Tai Meng and wept, saying, "People often told me Jun would surely rebel; I could not bear to wrong a man — Jun has indeed wronged me."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi summoned his general Tai Meng and said through tears, "People warned me again and again that Jun would rebel. I could not bring myself to wrong a loyal man—and Jun has wronged me."

sentences.zh: 吾思為將者非公莫可。

translations.literal: "I think for a general none but you will do."
translations.idiomatic: "I can think of no general but you for this task."

sentences.zh: 」濛頓首謝，率騎度江，為陣以行。

translations.literal: Meng kowtowed in thanks, led cavalry across the river, and advanced in formation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng kowtowed and led his cavalry across the river in battle formation.

sentences.zh: 士笑其怯，濛曰：「頵宿將多謀，備之何害？

translations.literal: Soldiers laughed at his timidity; Meng said, "Jun is a veteran of many stratagems — what harm in being prepared?"
translations.idiomatic: His men laughed at his caution. Meng said, "Jun is a veteran of many battles and much guile—what harm is there in being prepared?"

sentences.zh: 」與王壇等戰廣德，濛以行密書遺壇諸將，皆再拜氣奪。

translations.literal: At Guangde he fought Wang Tan and others; Meng sent Xingmi's letters to Tan's generals; all bowed twice and lost their spirit.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangde he fought Wang Tan and the others. Meng sent Xingmi's letters to Tan's generals, and they all bowed twice, their spirits broken.

sentences.zh: 濛麾兵擊之，壇走。

translations.literal: Meng waved the troops to attack; Tan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Meng waved his troops forward and Tan fled.

sentences.zh: 神福既以不戰困頵，頵紿言母病，還至蕪湖。

translations.literal: Shenfu having wearied Jun by not fighting, Jun lied that his mother was ill and returned to Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu had worn Jun down by refusing battle. Jun pretended his mother was ill and withdrew to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 聞壇敗，留精兵二萬屬郭行琮，身走城。

translations.literal: Hearing Tan was defeated, he left twenty thousand picked troops under Guo Xingzhen and himself fled to the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Tan had been defeated, he left twenty thousand elite troops with Guo Xingzhen and fled to the city himself.

sentences.zh: 濛之行，為狹營小舍，覘者以為才容二千人，頵輕之，不復召兵。

translations.literal: As Meng marched he built narrow camps and small shelters; observers thought they could hold only two thousand; Jun belittled him and did not recall more troops.
translations.idiomatic: As Meng advanced he built narrow camps and small shelters. Scouts thought he had no more than two thousand men. Jun despised him and did not call up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 與戰黃池，矢石始交而濛遁，兵爭逐北，遇伏，頵大敗，召蕪湖兵，不得入。

translations.literal: At Huangchi arrows and stones had just crossed when Meng fled; soldiers chased north in rivalry, met ambush — Jun was greatly defeated; he summoned Wuhu troops but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangchi the exchange of arrows had barely begun when Meng feigned flight. Jun's men rushed in pursuit and walked into an ambush. Jun was routed utterly. He called for his troops at Wuhu, but they could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 行琮及壇皆歸行密，頵恚，自料死士數百，號「爪牙都」，身薄戰。

translations.literal: Xingzhen and Tan all returned to Xingmi; Jun in rage mustered several hundred death soldiers called the "Claw-and-Fang Division" and pressed the fight himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhen and Tan both went over to Xingmi. Jun, enraged, gathered several hundred daredevils he called the Claw-and-Fang Division and led the charge himself.

sentences.zh: 濛退軍示弱，士超隍，濛殊死戰，軍潰。

translations.literal: Meng withdrew showing weakness; soldiers surmounted the rampart; Meng fought desperately; the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng withdrew as if in defeat. Jun's men scaled the ramparts. Meng turned and fought with desperate fury, and Jun's army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 頵奔城，橋陷，為亂兵所殺，年四十六。

translations.literal: Jun ran for the city; the bridge gave way; he was killed by mutinous troops, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Jun fled for the city, but the bridge collapsed beneath him and he was killed by his own disorderly troops. He was forty-six.

sentences.zh: 其下猶鬥，示頵首，乃潰。

translations.literal: His men still fought; when Jun's head was shown, they then broke.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought on until Jun's head was displayed; then they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 頵始以元瓘歸，戰不勝，輒欲殺之，頵母護免。

translations.literal: Initially when Yuan Guangzan was returned, whenever battle was lost Jun wished to kill him; Jun's mother protected and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Guangzan was first sent as hostage, Jun tried to kill him after every defeat, but Jun's mother always intervened to save him.

sentences.zh: 及镠與行密合，頵曰：「今日不勝，必殺元瓘。

translations.literal: When Liu and Xingmi joined forces, Jun said, "If we do not win today, I shall certainly kill Yuan Guangzan."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu and Xingmi joined forces, Jun said, "If we do not win today, I will kill Yuan Guangzan."

sentences.zh: 」已而頵死，傳首至淮南，行密泣下，葬以庶人禮，亦葬康儒，還元瓘於杭。

translations.literal: Then Jun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept, buried him with commoner's rites, also buried Kang Ru, returned Yuan Guangzan to Hang.
translations.idiomatic: Then Jun died. His head was sent to Huainan. Xingmi wept, buried him with the rites due a commoner, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guangzan to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 頵善為治，資寬厚，通利商賈，民愛之。

translations.literal: Jun was skilled in governance, generous and thick in resources, promoted merchants, and the people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was a capable administrator, generous in disposition, favorable to merchants, and beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 善遇士，若楊夔、康軿、夏侯淑、殷文圭、王希羽等皆為上客。

translations.literal: He treated scholars well — Yang Kui, Kang Zhen, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, Wang Xiyu and others were all honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: He treated men of letters with great respect. Yang Kui, Kang Zhen, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, Wang Xiyu, and others were all his honored guests.

sentences.zh: 文圭有美名，全忠、镠交辟不應。

translations.literal: Wengui had a fine reputation; Quanzhong and Liu both repeatedly invited him but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui enjoyed a fine reputation. Zhu Quanzhong and Qian Liu both invited him repeatedly, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 頵置田宅，迎其母，以甥事之，故文圭為盡力。

translations.literal: Jun set up fields and houses, welcomed his mother, treated him as a sister's son, so Wengui served with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Jun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him as a kinsman by marriage. Wengui therefore served him with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 夔知頵不足亢行密，著《溺賦》以戒，頵不用。

translations.literal: Kui knew Jun could not match Xingmi, wrote "Fu on Drowning" as a warning — Jun did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Kui knew Jun was no match for Xingmi and wrote the Fu on Drowning as a warning, but Jun paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 行密使王茂章穴地取潤州，安仁義以家屬保城樓，兵不敢登。

translations.literal: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel underground to take Runzhou; An Renyi placed his family on the city tower to guard it, and troops dared not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel under the walls to take Runzhou. An Renyi placed his family on the city tower as a shield, and the attackers dared not climb up.

sentences.zh: 召李德誠曰：「汝可以委命。

translations.literal: He summoned Li Decheng and said, "You may entrust your life."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Li Decheng and said, "You may answer for my life."

sentences.zh: 」乃抵弓矢就縛，父子斬揚州市。

translations.literal: He then handed over bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in Yangzhou market.
translations.idiomatic: He then laid down his bow and arrows and submitted to bonds. Father and son were beheaded in the market at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 濛，字頂雲，亦合肥人。

translations.literal: Meng, style name Dingyun, was also from Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, styled Dingyun, was also a native of Hefei.

sentences.zh: 頵破，行密表為檢校太保、宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: After Jun was defeated, Xingmi memorialized him as Acting Grand Guardian and inspector of Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun's defeat, Xingmi recommended Meng as Acting Grand Guardian and inspector of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianyou he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Tianyou era.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽者，廬州舒城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanhou was a native of Shucheng in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanhou was a native of Shucheng in Luz Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 事行密，破秦彥、畢師鐸、趙锽、孫儒功居多。

translations.literal: He served Xingmi; in defeating Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Chou, and Sun Ru his achievements were the greatest.
translations.idiomatic: He served Xingmi and won the greatest distinction in the defeats of Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Chou, and Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 行密欲以寬恕結人心，而延壽敢殺。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to bind hearts through leniency, but Yanhou dared to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wished to win hearts through mercy, but Yanhou was quick to kill.

sentences.zh: 時揚州多盜，捕得者，行密輒賜所盜遣之，戒曰：「勿使延壽知。

translations.literal: At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when captured, Xingmi would return what they stole and send them away, warning, "Do not let Yanhou know."
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous in Yangzhou. When one was caught, Xingmi would return what he had stolen and send him away, warning, "Do not let Yanhou know."

sentences.zh: 」已而陰許延壽殺之。

translations.literal: Then secretly he permitted Yanhou to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Then secretly he allowed Yanhou to execute them.

sentences.zh: 初，壽州刺史高彥溫舉州入朱全忠，行密襲之，諸將憚城堅不可拔，延壽鼓之，拔其城即表為淮南節度副使。

translations.literal: Initially Shouzhou prefect Gao Yanwen surrendered the prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi raided it; the generals feared the strong walls could not be taken; Yanhou urged them on, took the city, and was immediately memorialized as Huainan military deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the prefect of Shouzhou, Gao Yanwen, had surrendered his prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong. Xingmi attacked it, but his generals feared the strong walls could not be taken. Yanhou roused them, captured the city, and was at once recommended as deputy military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶屯壽春，延壽以新軍出，每旗五伍為列，遣李厚以十旗擊西偏，不勝，將斬之，厚請益五旗，殊死戰，全忠引去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong still encamped at Shouchun; Yanhou led fresh troops out, each banner with five squads in a column; sent Li Hou with ten banners to attack the west flank, did not win, was about to behead him; Hou asked for five more banners, fought desperately, Quanzhong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was still encamped at Shouchun. Yanhou led his fresh troops out with five men to each banner. He sent Li Hou with ten banners against the western flank. When Hou was beaten, Yanhou was about to execute him, but Hou begged for five more banners and fought to the death until Quanzhong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 於是取黃、蘄、光三州，以功遷壽州團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Huang, Qi, and Guang prefectures; for merit was transferred to Shouzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Huang, Qi, and Guang prefectures and, for his merit, was made defense commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在鳳翔，詔延壽圍蔡以披全忠勢，擢奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang; ordered Yanhou to besiege Cai to relieve Quanzhong's pressure; promoted to military governor of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang, he ordered Yanhou to besiege Cai and relieve the pressure on Quanzhong, and promoted him to military governor of the Fengguo Army.

sentences.zh: 全忠兵每至，延壽開門不設備，而不敢逼也。

translations.literal: Whenever Quanzhong's troops came, Yanhou opened the gates without preparing defenses, yet they dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Quanzhong's troops appeared, Yanhou would open his gates without taking precautions, yet they dared not press him.

sentences.zh: 延壽用軍常以寡鬥眾，敗還者盡斬之。

translations.literal: Yanhou used troops often fighting few against many; those who returned defeated were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhou often fought with few against many, and any soldier who returned defeated was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 田頵之附全忠，延壽陰約曰：「公有所為，我願執鞭。

translations.literal: When Tian Jun attached himself to Quanzhong, Yanhou secretly pledged, saying, "Whatever you undertake, I wish to hold the whip."
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Jun threw in his lot with Quanzhong, Yanhou secretly pledged, "Whatever you undertake, I am ready to serve at your side."

sentences.zh: 」頵喜，二人謀絕行密。

translations.literal: Jun was pleased; the two plotted to break with Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was delighted, and the two plotted to break with Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密憂甚，紿病目，行觸柱僵。

translations.literal: Xingmi was deeply worried, feigned illness of the eyes, walked and struck a pillar and collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was deeply troubled. He pretended to be blind, walked into a pillar, and collapsed as if stunned.

sentences.zh: 妻，延壽姊也，掖之。

translations.literal: His wife was Yanhou's elder sister; she supported him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, who was Yanhou's elder sister, helped him up.

sentences.zh: 行密泣曰：「吾喪明，諸子幼，得舅代我，無憂矣。

translations.literal: Xingmi wept and said, "I have lost my sight, my sons are young — with my uncle-in-law to replace me, no worries."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wept and said, "I have gone blind, my sons are still young—if my uncle-in-law will take my place, I need fear nothing."

sentences.zh: 」遣辯士召之，延壽疑，不肯赴。

translations.literal: He sent an eloquent envoy to summon him; Yanhou suspected and would not come.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an eloquent envoy to summon him, but Yanhou was suspicious and refused to come.

sentences.zh: 姊遣婢報故，延壽疾走揚州，拜未訖，士禽殺之，而廢其妻。

translations.literal: His sister sent a maid to report the truth; Yanhou rushed to Yangzhou; before his bow was finished, soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: His sister sent a maid to tell him the truth. Yanhou raced to Yangzhou, but before his bow was complete soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：全忠，唐之盜也，行密誌梟其元而後已。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Quanzhong was Tang's bandit; Xingmi resolved to behead him before he would stop.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Quanzhong was a robber of the Tang. Xingmi was resolved not to rest until he had taken Quanzhong's head.

sentences.zh: 田頵使出軍賦而助之，此其謀責難而絕之，非忠於唐也。

translations.literal: Tian Jun sent out military levies to aid him — here his scheme was to reproach and break with him, not loyalty to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Jun sent troops and supplies to aid Quanzhong, his aim was to reproach and break with Xingmi—not loyalty to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 棄所附而覬尊大，亦已妄矣。

translations.literal: To abandon those he followed and covet greatness — already reckless.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon one's patron and reach for supremacy was folly enough.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱孟公綽為趙、魏老則優，不可以為滕、薛大夫。

translations.literal: Confucius said Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward for Zhao and Wei, but could not serve as minister for Teng and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said that Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward for the great houses of Zhao and Wei, but could not serve as minister in small states like Teng and Xue.

sentences.zh: 如仁厚、田、朱，材不足為吳、蜀之老，可與事天子哉！

translations.literal: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu — their talent was insufficient to be elders of Wu and Shu; could they serve the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu lacked the talent to be chief stewards even in Wu and Shu—how could they serve the Son of Heaven!
